summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for an allogeneic matched unrelated donor stem cell transplant as part of a clinical trial for EBV-positive classical Hodgkin lymphoma. She had completed prior chemotherapy and was in remission. A central venous catheter was placed on admission, followed by reduced-intensity conditioning with fludarabine and busulfan. The stem cell infusion occurred on May 17th without complications. Engraftment was achieved by day 28, with rising neutrophil counts. She developed mild gastrointestinal graft-versus-host disease, presenting as watery ostomy output, and was treated with budesonide. Her C. difficile infection was managed with ongoing oral vancomycin due to immunosuppression. Blood glucose was elevated, requiring insulin adjustment by the diabetes team. Tacrolimus and sirolimus levels were monitored and dosed appropriately. She remained infection-free, with negative CMV and blood cultures. She was discharged home on immunosuppressive, antimicrobial, and supportive therapies with close follow-up planned.
problems: Hodgkin's disease, unspecified type, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
